articles.headline: Tyrese Haliburton scores 7 in 1st game in more than 16 months
articles.description: Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton scored seven points during his 16 minutes of action against the Wolves on Wednesday. It was his first game in more than 16 months, as Haliburton was recovering from a torn Achilles.
articles.headlineJa: タイリーズ・ハリバートン、16か月ぶりの復帰戦で7得点
articles.descriptionJa: ペイサーズのスター、タイリーズ・ハリバートンは水曜日のウルブズ戦で16分間出場し、7得点を記録した。アキレス腱断裂からの回復を経て、16か月以上ぶりの試合出場となった。
articles.body:
AMES, Iowa -- Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton said he felt like he was playing too fast during Indiana's 123-112 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves in its preseason opener at Iowa State on Wednesday night, Haliburton's first game in more than 16 months.

He scored seven points on 3-of-8 shooting with six assists, one steal and two blocks during his 16 minutes of action.

"It's the first game, but it's got to slow down," Haliburton said Wednesday night. "There was just a lot of adrenaline. I was hyped to be out there, excited, but I just got to slow down a little bit."

Haliburton compared himself to a rookie after the game, but he took solace in the fact that although his body was moving too fast, he felt like he could read the floor at his usual speed.

"It'll happen with time," he said. "The only way to really replicate that is game reps against other guys. And that's what that was. So really excited about it.

"There's a ton of improvement that there is to be made on my end and on our team's end, but just excited to be back on the floor."

It had been more than 400 days since Haliburton's last NBA game, when he tore his right Achilles during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. He struggled to sleep last night, but he said that had more to do with the anticipation of playing his first game back at Iowa State, where he played for two years in college from 2018 to 2020.

The Pacers had initially scheduled this game for the 2025 preseason, but with Haliburton sidelined last season, the game got pushed back one year.

Haliburton wanted to replicate a college atmosphere Wednesday night, so he bought out the student section at both ends of the arena, so seats were available to students on a first come, first serve basis, prompting a line that wrapped around the block of the arena hours before tipoff. The fans at the front of the line said they began lining up at 11 p.m. the night before.

"It's the loudest preseason game I've ever been a part of," Haliburton said. "But had a lot of fun, a lot of special memories I've made here and that just adds to it."

Haliburton played all of his 16 minutes during the first half, but fans inside Hilton Coliseum wanted more of the Pacers star.

With Haliburton sitting on the bench during the fourth quarter, fans began to chant "We want Hali."

Haliburton responded by pointing to his feet. His basketball shoes had been left in the locker room, and he was wearing white sandals and socks, a signal that he was done for the night.

"Put your shoes on," the next chant began. Haliburton laughed after the game and said he wasn't tempted.

"Hell no," Haliburton said after the game with a laugh. "I appreciate that the students wanted that as they should, but we have a process."

articles.headline: Tyreek Hill's wife cross-examined during Day 2 of trial
articles.description: Tyreek Hill's attorneys tried to show discrepancies in the testimony of his wife and police photos of her after a '24 incident to try to discredit abuse claims.
articles.headlineJa: 公判2日目、タイリーク・ヒルの妻が反対尋問を受ける
articles.descriptionJa: タイリーク・ヒルの弁護団は、虐待の主張の信憑性を揺るがすため、妻の証言と24年の事件後の警察による写真との間に矛盾があることを示そうとした。
articles.body:
MIAMI -- Tyreek Hill's wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro, faced intense cross-examination on the second day of a civil assault and battery trial against the former All-Pro wide receiver.

Attorneys for Hill on Wednesday attempted to show discrepancies in Vaccaro's testimony and used police photos of her after a January 2024 incident to try to discredit her claims that he had physically abused her.

Hill's attorney, Michael Gottlieb, showed jurors photos of Vaccaro taken from various angles by police after an alleged altercation with her husband in an Orlando, Florida, hotel. Under cross-examination, she acknowledged the photos -- in which she was wearing a short-sleeve T-shirt and black pants -- did not show any red marks, bruising or scratches on her body or face. But Vaccaro told the court that she looked "beat down" in the photos.

Gottlieb continued by asking if Vaccaro took photos of injuries after any of the alleged incidents with Hill. Vaccaro said she did not because she "wasn't trying to collect evidence."

The questioning got heated on occasion, with the judge admonishing Gottlieb multiple times for interrupting Vaccaro while she tried to answer questions during the nearly three-hour cross-examination.

During the questioning, Hill showed little reaction, occasionally snacking on what appeared to be candy or pretzels as he sat next to another defense attorney.

At one point during the cross-examination, Gottlieb read jurors a text message Vaccaro sent to her husband shortly before the birth of their daughter that said, "I am so grateful for you, babe. Thank you for everything you do for our family and for making this pregnancy such a beautiful and special journey."

The attorney tried repeatedly to undermine her credibility by juxtaposing her descriptions of violence and personal crisis against outward expressions of normalcy. Vaccaro told jurors she was about to have a baby and wanted to "keep the family intact" and be on "good terms" with Hill.

Gottlieb repeatedly asked Vaccaro why she didn't tell anyone about the alleged abuse. She testified that the "police, and pediatrician, OB-GYN" were all "so starstruck, every single one of them" with the former Dolphins wide receiver that she didn't want to embarrass him. She said "it wasn't something I wanted to publicly say. It was hard for me to even say this now."

Vaccaro said people were so enamored with Hill that a doctor asked for a selfie with him while Vaccaro was in labor with their daughter.

Vaccaro said the turning point for her came during an April 6, 2024, confrontation the couple had in their daughter's room at their Miami-area condominium. The encounter was caught on a nanny camera while their daughter was napping. Vaccaro's mother was present at the time and witnessed the encounter.

articles.headline: Vikings' Justin Jefferson says plan is to play vs. Saints
articles.description: Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson returned to practice Wednesday on a limited basis for the first time since spraining his left ankle 10 days ago and appeared optimistic that he will play Sunday at New Orleans.
articles.headlineJa: バイキングスのジャスティン・ジェファーソン、セインツ戦への出場を予定
articles.descriptionJa: バイキングスのレシーバー、ジャスティン・ジェファーソンが水曜日に練習に復帰した。10日前に左足首を捻挫して以来、初めての練習となるが制限付きでの参加となった。ニューオーリンズでの日曜日の試合に出場することに対し、楽観的な見方を示している。
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson returned to practice Wednesday on a limited basis for the first time since spraining his left ankle 10 days ago and appeared optimistic that he will play Sunday against the New Orleans Saints.

"The plan is for me to play," Jefferson said. "But who knows? We're going to take it day by day."

Jefferson suffered the injury in the first quarter of the Vikings' 23-16 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sept. 28 and missed all of Sunday's 15-10 victory against the Miami Dolphins.

He has long had the Saints game circled on his personal calendar because it will be his first chance to play in front of a full NFL crowd in his home state of Louisiana. The Vikings last played in New Orleans during the 2020 season, when attendance was limited by COVID-19 protocols.

"Being back at home, being back in Louisiana is definitely something that I want to do," he said.

Jefferson has caught 13 passes for 179 yards and two touchdowns. But his ankle injury, and quarterback Kyler Murray's Week 1 concussion, have limited them to 18 snaps together.

That's among the reasons Jefferson is pushing to play this week, rather than sit and take advantage of the Vikings' Week 6 bye to continue healing.

"I want to be out there," Jefferson said. "That's the main thing. I hate missing games. I hated missing last week. I wanted to be out there last week, and especially at home, and I never want to miss any time. So it's been a little tough. They've been holding me back a little bit, just not trying to force anything, but being able to be out there [at practice], it just feels good."

articles.headline: Broncos' Payton: Concerned about details, not playcalling
articles.description: Sean Payton said righting the wrongs of Denver's offense is more about the "specific and the detail of each play," not who is actually calling the plays.
articles.headlineJa: ブロンコスのペイトン、懸念しているのはプレーコールではなく「細部」
articles.descriptionJa: ショーン・ペイトンは、デンバーの攻撃陣を立て直すには、誰がプレーコールを行うかよりも、「各プレーの具体性と詳細」が重要であると語った。
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- As Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton answered question after question about the team's offensive struggles Wednesday, including on quarterback Bo Nix's play and the possible solutions for it, he arrived at a bottom line: "Certainly this isn't championship football, what we see.''

The Broncos (2-2) rank near the bottom of the league in scoring (27th), total yards per game (27th), rushing yards per game (29th), passing yards per game (20th), QBR (23rd) and Offensive EPA (22nd).

As the queries about the offense came, Payton said, "I was having a good Wednesday, I felt like I was having a good Wednesday.''

He was asked about the first four games with offensive coordinator Davis Webb as the playcaller and whether that was a big enough sample size for Payton to determine if he needs to call plays again, as he had done throughout his tenure as an NFL head coach before this season.

"I think our focus needs to be more on the specific and the detail of each play regardless [of who's calling the plays],'' Payton said. "I think Davis is very fast, very quick and understands what we're doing. I think that the most important job I have is really evaluating the whys. I think collectively, we all, after a game, and after a four-game sample size, certainly this isn't championship football, what we see. How quickly can we correct those things?''

Nix is 22nd in the league in QBR (46.1) and 27th in average air yards per attempt (5.9). The lack of big plays on offense overall has become a four-game trend; the Broncos are 29th in plays of 20-or-more yards and 30th in explosive plays with 16 (runs of at least 10 yards, pass plays of at least 20 yards).

In Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, running back RJ Harvey led Denver in both targets (10) and receptions (10) as he averaged 6.8 yards per catch.

Payton said Wednesday he believes it all tracks to "the details, the little things,'' rather than some substantial shift in approach on offense.

Wide receiver Courtland Sutton, who has nine catches combined in four games, said Wednesday he believes Nix has taken an unfair amount of outside criticism so far this season.

"We all got our hand in it,'' Sutton said. "... We all have our hand in this pot ... He's not the only one out there when we go play ... we all have accountability.''

Said Nix: "You don't want to listen to too many things, the noise, that's not going to do anything for you. You want to make sure you're listening to your coaches, your teammates, the people who are actually trying to make you better and understand a little more of what's going on and that sort of thing. For me, it's all about who you're giving your attention to.''

articles.headline: TE Sam LaPorta says extension talks with Lions at 'stalemate'
articles.description: Lions tight end Sam LaPorta is currently focused on the 2026 season but acknowledged for the first time after Wednesday's practice that he has broken off contract talks on an extension.
articles.headlineJa: ライオンズのTEサム・ラポータ、契約延長交渉は「膠着状態」と明かす
articles.descriptionJa: ライオンズのタイトエンド、サム・ラポータは現在2026年シーズンに集中しているが、水曜日の練習後、契約延長に関する交渉が中断していることを初めて認めた。
articles.body:
ALLEN PARK, Mich. -- Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta is currently focused on the 2026 season but acknowledged for the first time after Wednesday's practice that he has broken off contract talks on an extension.

LaPorta says he would like to think that he's optimistic about reaching a new deal but is also unsure if things will get worked out before he's set to become a free agent in 2027.

"I don't know if it's truly off the table, but I think there's certainly a stalemate right now and I'm really giving the reigns to my agent Jack Bechta," LaPorta said. "He's been handling it with the front office and all the advice he's given me so far is just that we haven't come to terms yet. That's about it."

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that the Lions and LaPorta have broken off contract talks.

The Lions have been trying to work out a long-term deal with LaPorta for the first few weeks but have yet to agree to terms. After selecting him in the second round of the 2023 NFL draft out of Iowa, the Lions would have the franchise tag available as well.

After undergoing surgery in November to repair a fully herniated disk, and missing the final eight games of the 2025 season, LaPorta has returned to the mix to be a big part of the offense under new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing.

The 25-year-old has logged the third-most receiving yards (228) with two touchdowns through the first four games.

Although the Lions fell to 2-2 after a 32-26 loss to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, head coach Dan Campbell described his 8-reception, 84-yard performance as LaPorta's best game of the season, and he also finished with a touchdown.

Campbell feels that his "production speaks for itself" but has shied away from focusing on the LaPorta's business with the organization.

"All that stuff, man, that's the last thing on my mind right now is what's going on with all that," Campbell said. "Man, there's always going to be two sides, and you work through these things and just because there's a report of that doesn't mean that that's some big issue, big deal. I love LaPorta. We love LaPorta. He's a heck of a football player."

For LaPorta, it's not important to be the highest-paid tight end in the league, but he would like to be paid his value. Bechta, his agent, also represents Tucker Kraft, who agreed to a four-year, $75 million contract before the season with the Green Bay Packers.

"I've never hung my hat on being the highest-paid tight end, being the first tight end to get drafted in my class, making the Pro Bowl, being First-Team All-Pro," LaPorta said. "I've always put all my chips in the pile of 'What can I do for the team?' And those chips are still all there. Like I said, I'm letting my agent and the front office handle the financial side of things."

articles.headline: Giants' Malik Nabers has 'sore' knee, doesn't practice
articles.description: Giants star wide receiver Malik Nabers did not practice Wednesday because of a knee injury, saying only he was more "sore" than usual.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツのマリック・ネイバーズ、膝に「痛み」を訴え練習を欠場
articles.descriptionJa: ジャイアンツのスターワイドレシーバー、マリック・ネイバーズは膝の負傷により水曜日の練習を欠場した。本人は、いつもより「痛み」が強いだけだと話している。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants star wide receiver Malik Nabers did not practice Wednesday because of a knee injury, saying only he was more "sore" than usual.

He exited the Giants' first practice of the week Wednesday and sat on a medicine ball and talked to team trainers during the open portion of practice. The Pro Bowl receiver seemed to be walking with a slight limp when the two-hour practice was over.

"Just sore," Nabers said at the podium moments later. "Just sore. We'll see how the next day goes, but through the week, I'm usually sore. But this one was kind of a little bit more sore. I always continue to fight through it."

The Giants could use him in the lineup for Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders after already having lost Braxton Berrios to a season-ending foot injury.

Nabers tore the ACL in his right knee last season and needed a cleanup procedure earlier this year. He returned to the practice field for the start of training camp and was ready for the opener.

He had his most productive game since returning from the injury Sunday when he caught six passes on seven targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Arizona Cardinals.

Coach John Harbaugh didn't seem too worried about his No. 1 receiver.

"He's doing great, yeah," Harbaugh said. "He had a great day. Great spirits [Wednesday]. He had a good workday."

When told that Nabers said he was sore, Harbaugh barely flinched.

"I'll take him at his word then," he said.

Nabers isn't the Giants' only injury concern. Defensive lineman Chauncey Golston has a recurring neck problem that Harbaugh said "could" shut him down for significant time. The Giants and Golston are exploring all their options.

Nabers, who leads the Giants with 208 receiving yards this season, talked just last week about gaining more trust in his knee. He admitted at the start of the season that he was rusty, and he failed to reach 100 yards through the first three games.

He seemed to know that a breakout game was coming. On Sunday, it still wasn't enough for his liking when the Giants and starting quarterback Jameis Winston fed him the ball. Nabers was seen at times animatedly talking toward the sideline from the field. He thought they left some out there.

"I felt like I didn't get targeted much after halftime," said Nabers, who had one catch on two targets for 28 yards in the second half. "So, that was just a thing. It's just ... I felt like creating explosives down the field was just helping us get in a better position to score touchdowns. Some of those plays didn't come my way, so just trying to figure out why."

Harbaugh said they talked after the game, brushing it off as Nabers being emotional and competitive.

articles.headline: Commanders' Jayden Daniels fully practices, trending toward return
articles.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels continued on a path that is expected to result in him playing Sunday against the New York Giants, only three weeks after he dislocated his elbow.
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels continued on a path that is expected to result in him playing Sunday against the New York Giants, only three weeks after he dislocated his elbow.

Daniels was a full participant in practice, as coach Dan Quinn said he would be all week with the idea that he'll play when the Commanders (1-3) face the Giants (3-1).

Daniels said he knew he was ready to return after being a limited participant in practice when the team trained in London ahead of a loss to the Colts.

"I felt good," Daniels said, adding that practicing allowed him to "give myself opportunities to go out there and play on Sunday."

Daniels will have to wear a brace on his left elbow the rest of the season.

"I'm going to embrace the brace, not worry about it too much," Daniels said. "It's my non-throwing arm, so, I think as long as I got the right one to attack, I'll be all right."

His return became even more important when his backup, Marcus Mariota, sprained his right medial collateral ligament. He's expected to miss the next two games and then return after the Week 7 bye.

Daniels will wear a brace that will keep his left elbow slightly bent, with the idea that it can prevent another dislocation.

"Just trying to get used to it," Daniels said. "It's just a part of me now, so, you know, for the time being, as long as I'm on that field, just getting used to it, trying to find the different ways where it's most comfortable and I'm not really just thinking about it. I'm just out there playing."

His return can provide a boost to a team that needs one.

"He gives us that spark, that extra juice knowing we've got our guy back there," tight end Chig Okonkwo said.

During the portion of practice open to the media, Daniels took snaps from center Lucas Patrick in warmups and threw with more zip than last week. In other drills, a coach, kneeling, would hand the ball to Daniels, who took it with both hands and would pitch it to a running back.

Daniels dislocated the elbow on the final play of the first half in a Week 2 loss at Dallas, when guard Chris Paul inadvertently stepped on Daniels' foot as he backed away from center on a third-and-goal from the 1-yard line.

As Daniels fell back, he planted his left arm on the ground to brace his fall; it then dislocated. After seeing multiple specialists, Daniels said he was "at peace" with his decision to play.

"I want to play football," he said.

But when asked if he'd run the same as in the past, he responded, "Is it the fourth quarter? If it's the fourth quarter, we've got to do something to win, right?"

He later said, "There's ways you could talk about different ways of protecting myself. But I don't, I don't get hit in practice, so I wouldn't know till Sunday."

articles.headline: Scott McTominay back in Napoli training after heart procedure
articles.description: Scott McTominay has returned to training with Napoli for the first time since undergoing a heart procedure last month.
articles.body:
Scott McTominay has returned to training with Napoli for the first time since undergoing a heart procedure last month.

The Scotland international, 29, received corrective ablation treatment in the Spire Manchester Hospital after being diagnosed with a mild, benign arrhythmia in September.

The procedure was declared a success, with the midfielder prescribed a period of rest before rejoining the Serie A side. He had previously taken to social media to tell fans "See you soon Napoli, I won't take long."

The club confirmed on Wednesday that he had been cleared for duty after further checkups and posted pictures of him working alongside teammates ahead of their weekend clash against Frosinone.

A short update read: "On Wednesday, Scott McTominay underwent further diagnostic tests, which showed that he is fit to play. [He] therefore resumed training with the rest of the team after the period spent training separately."

The former Manchester United man has played twice this season, coming off after 56 minutes against Como before his heart issue was detected. He missed the next three games as well as the recent international break with Scotland.

articles.headline: Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo in doubt for Liverpool vs. Man City clash
articles.description: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has cast doubt on the chances of Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo being fit to face Manchester City this weekend.
articles.headlineJa: リヴァプール対マン・シティ戦、アレクサンダー・イサクとコディ・ガクポの出場が危ぶれる
articles.descriptionJa: リヴァプールのアンドニ・イラオラ監督は、今週末のマンチェスター・シティ戦に向けて、アレクサンダー・イサクとコディ・ガクポが万全の状態で出場できるかどうかに疑問を呈した。
articles.body:
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has cast doubt on the chances of Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo being fit to face Manchester City this weekend.

The pair both returned home early from international duty with Sweden and the Netherlands due to thigh and ankle problems, respectively.

- Liverpool can't afford to be without Isak, Gakpo for daunting October fixture list

- Mock draft: How would Premier League teams pick if Man City cheating scandal took a turn?

- How top Premier League clubs view Man City's guilty verdict

Having inherited Hugo Ekitike's long-term Achilles injury, Iraola could be without his two senior forwards for Sunday's highly-anticipated clash, City's first match since an independent commission found them guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

"I think Alex Isak and Cody Gakpo both have had to leave the national teams with injuries," Iraola told beIN SPORTS.

"Now it's a matter of if they are going to recover in time to help us in the next game or not. But right now they are both injured."

Iraola did not mention the status of center back Jérémy Jacquet, who was omitted from France's 4-1 victory over Belgium on Monday with a hamstring strain.

The visit of City is the biggest game of Iraola's Liverpool career so far and despite four wins and three draws his side have struggled to find anything close to their best form.

"We've been unbeaten but they've won all of them, so it makes a big difference in their side," he said. "I think we need to be very, very good if we want to beat City because they've been especially offensively scoring a lot of goals lately.

"We know the names that are very dangerous. But I think also we've shown good defensive improvements lately and I hope we can defend the threats that they have and also hurt them on the other side."

The international break will have done little to help the consistency Iraola needs as he tries to get a squad which hugely underperformed last season to successfully adopt his methods.

"I think the goal is quite clear and I think everyone understands what we are trying to build," he said. "Try to be more intense, more vertical, but also you want to control the games.

"For example, I think in Newcastle [a 2-2 draw] we played a good game but probably we conceded two goals in transition [and] you want to control a little bit more of the games.

"I think lately we've been controlling the games much more but we lacked a little bit [of] this offensive fluidity that we had in the first game. So, now it's a matter of balancing this a little.

"Obviously we want to attack very well and defend very well but sometimes you have to choose or you have to adapt the team to what you prefer or what is the requirements of a specific game and we are trying to balance all this."

articles.headline: Another bad Man United run has Carrick feeling the heat. Should he be?
articles.description: Michael Carrick is hardly unique in that he brought hope to Man United, but is he on course to become the latest coach to be fired midseason?
articles.headlineJa: マン・Uの再びの不調でキャリックにプレッシャー。解任されるべきか？
articles.descriptionJa: マイケル・キャリックがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドに希望をもたらしたことは決して珍しいことではないが、彼はシーズン途中で解任される最新の監督となってしまうのだろうか？
articles.body:
For many supporters, the Manchester United cycle appears to be back in full swing. An uptick in form under Michael Carrick renewed hope that the club could finally be moving in the right direction toward the end of the 2025-26 campaign, but it has been followed by a difficult start to the new season and pressure is mounting on the head coach.

It was a similar story for José Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim. Moments of optimism -- some briefer than others -- and then a sharp downturn that led to a seemingly inevitable parting of ways.

United have sacked managers midway through each of their past two seasons -- Ten Hag in October 2024 and Amorim in January 2026. Take it back further and managers have been dismissed midseason in four of the past eight completed campaigns. The scrutiny on Carrick -- who signed only a two-year contract as long-term head coach in May -- has increased with United winning just two of their first seven games in all competitions.

A last-minute equalizer to secure a 1-1 draw at Fulham before the international break prevented a run of three defeats in a row but Carrick -- and the club in general -- is under the spotlight again.

The international break has been dominated by Manchester City and their legal case with the Premier League. United could end up with millions in compensation, but the most immediate -- and welcome -- consequence of the verdict breaking is that the spotlight has been focused on the Etihad and not Old Trafford.

Will that remain the case after Saturday's visit of Tottenham Hotspur, another club in turmoil? Or do we have reason to doubt Carrick's position as manager?

Is history repeating?

There's certainly a familiar feel about it all. Ten Hag was sacked after United won four of their 13 games in all competitions to open the 2024-25 season. Amorim survived a start of two wins from seven but was gone by January.

Solskjaer lasted 17 games in 2021-22 despite finishing second the season before. Mourinho also finished second in 2017-18 but was dismissed just 24 games into the 2018-19 campaign. It's evidence of how quickly things can unravel at Old Trafford.

Carrick won 12 of 17 games last season after being appointed caretaker boss in January, suffering just two defeats and recording impressive wins over Manchester City, Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool along the way. No Premier League manager won more points during the same period as United finished third to qualify for the UEFA Champions League.

But just like the achievements of Mourinho and Solskjaer, it has been quickly forgotten. The defeat to newly promoted Hull City on the opening weekend put Carrick on the back foot immediately. The performance against 10-man Manchester City was poor, and losing to Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup after leading 2-0 after 10 minutes was damaging.

articles.headline: Tottenham's Mathys Tel equals France under-21 goalscoring record
articles.description: Mathys Tel will be hoping to take his goal-scoring exploits with France Under-21s over the international break into Tottenham's fight to turn their Premier League season around.
articles.headlineJa: トッテナムのマティス・テル、フランスU-21の得点記録に並ぶ
articles.descriptionJa: マティス・テルは、代表ウィーク中のフランスU-21での得点感覚を、プレミアリーグのシーズン立て直しに向けたトッテナムの戦いに持ち込みたいと考えている。
articles.body:
Mathys Tel will be hoping to take his goal-scoring exploits with France Under-21s over the international break into Tottenham's fight to turn their Premier League season around.

Tel has yet to score for Spurs this season but hit a hat-trick in a 7-1 win over Switzerland in Orleans on Tuesday night as France, who had already qualified for the 2027 European U21 Championship, completed their group campaign unbeaten with eight victories.

With 17 goals, Tel, who also scored in two other games over the break, has equalled Odsonne Edouard's record for France U21s and could have put himself into contention for a senior call-up to Zinedine Zidane's squad for the Nations League games in November.

"My brother had been nagging me about it [the goals record] for months. In the end it was in the back of my mind," Tel told reporters, as quoted in L'Equipe.

"With qualification [achieved], there was a different kind of motivation that allowed me to give my best, so now I am very happy."

Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham slumped to the bottom of the table ahead of the international break, with a 3-2 home defeat by Aston Villa a third loss from their five opening Premier League games.

The boss welcomed former player and first-team coach Gus Poyet to the training ground on Tuesday and appeared in good spirits as the pair chatted on the sidelines in a video on the club's social media account.

Spurs travel to Manchester United on Saturday and have a few fitness concerns following the international break.

- Premier League depth charts for most popular teams: Who is key?

- Man City mock draft: How Premier League teams could pick in hypothetical punishment

Right-back Pedro Porro has been carrying a hamstring injury which saw him pull out the Spain squad ahead of the extended three-week window.

Defender Jan Paul van Hecke was then sent home early from the Netherlands camp with a foot problem, which could keep him out of contention at Old Trafford.

Fellow Dutchman Micky van de Ven picked up a minor hand injury after being accidentally stepped on during the win over Serbia in Eindhoven and was forced off late on, but the Spurs captain is expected to be involved.

Speaking after the match, Netherlands manager Xavi told reporters: "He is okay. He felt dizzy because he suffered with his finger. It is not a big injury."

articles.headline: We don't get Man City guilty verdict without hacker Rui Pinto, but it doesn't make him a hero
articles.description: The Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its core, wouldn't have been possible without Football Leaks and its founder, Rui Pinto. However, he is a complicated figure, with light and dark to his actions.
articles.headlineJa: ハッカーのルイ・ピントがいなければマン・シティの有罪判決はなかったが、彼がヒーローなわけではない
articles.descriptionJa: イングランドのサッカー界を根底から揺るがしているマンチェスター・シティの事案は、「フットボール・リークス」とその創設者ルイ・ピントがいなければ不可能だっただろう。しかし、彼の行動には光と影があり、複雑な人物である。
articles.body:
It's worth reminding ourselves that the Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its foundation, would never have seen the light of day without a spiky-haired college dropout turned self-taught hacker named Rui Pinto.

Had he not obtained and shared more than 70 million documents with the German magazine Der Spiegel starting in 2016, culminating in the publication of their massive "Football Leaks" investigation two years later, there would have been no investigation of City -- not by UEFA, not by the Premier League, not by any of the other bodies that may get involved once the current process is concluded.

Simply put, there would have been no legal basis for anyone to do this. We would have had an alternate reading of history -- one where City get new owners, Abu Dhabi United Group in 2009, spend a ton of money, watch their revenues skyrocket and dominate the game, all the while complying with every single financial regulation set before them. (The only exception was in 2014, when they breached UEFA's Financial Fair Play regulations and eventually signed a three-year settlement agreement.)

Whatever the ultimate outcome of the City case -- whether it results in expulsion from the Premier League and Sheikh Mansour having to shell out hundreds of millions in fines and compensation, or somehow ends in the club getting most, if not all, of the charges overturned on appeal -- this should be a massive wake-up call to those running the game. The message: football needs better oversight and more transparency.

Whichever way the dust settles, this much is obvious: the system failed. Either City did participate in a massive "sham" (to quote from the verdict), effectively cheating while the system failed to notice and act, or the Premier League is so inept that it has somehow been duped by a conspiracy of legacy clubs into conducting an ultimately futile eight-year investigation. Neither outcome is good; in fact, both are embarrassingly bad for the world's most successful league.

What would better oversight and transparency look like? How about something like we have in the NFL, where information about salaries, sponsorships and other revenue is shared not just with the league, but with teams around the league itself as well as the players' union. That creates a virtuous cycle of self-policing and makes it much harder to engage in financial skullduggery. (Harder, but not impossible, as old-school San Francisco 49ers fans will confirm.)

In the Premier League, far too much is a closely guarded secret in the name of "competitive advantage" -- clubs, not just City, disclose as little as legally allowed as if they were running some normal business, not a hugely important public trust like the world's most popular sport.

All of which brings us back to Pinto.
